readerQuestion: Will my charitable donations lower my taxes in 2026, and by how much?
demandSource: DataForSEO measured 590/mo KD 16 for 'charitable donation tax deduction calculator' and 'charitable contribution deduction calculator'; autocomplete 'church donation tax deduction calculator' (estimate 75/mo, not measured)
decisionGap: Existing church guide explains rules and one bunching example in prose; reader cannot enter own AGI/gifts to see whether giving changes their bill. No calculator existed (reviewer-verified).

inputsSourced.nonItemizerCap: Public Law 119-21: $1,000 / $2,000 MFJ, cash only (per IRS search result, final Pub 526 2026 not retrieved)

findings.label: calculated
findings.text: MFJ $150k AGI, $12k cash gifts, $20k other itemized: standard route wins; giving adds $2,000 of deductions; $440 saved at 22%

findings.label: calculated
findings.text: Bunching $24k into year one adds $7,050 of two-year deductions (about $1,551 at 22%); reproduces the church guide's published example

counterexample: Single, AGI $20k, $15k gifts, $20k other itemized: bunching $30k is capped by the 60% limit and loses $11,900 of deductions versus giving evenly
unknowns: IRS has not published a 2026 worksheet for the order of the 60% limit and 0.5% floor; tool applies 60% first, page says so
final 2026 Pub 526 text not read (fetched 2025 edition only)
wouldChangeRecommendation: A different ordering of limit vs floor in final IRS guidance; a bunched gift over 60% of AGI; other itemized deductions far below the standard deduction
medium: interactive calculator with on-page worked scenarios; key answer readable without interaction (intro worked example + howItWorks scenarios)

provenance.scopeAndLimits: internal modeling of the tool's own formula on stated scenarios; not a product test; no client records
provenance.publicMethod: on-page howItWorks states formulas, scenarios and assumptions; the calculator above lets readers re-run them
